publish.title: Why you stopped getting stronger (progressive overload)
publish.description: A simple explanation of progressive overload and four ways to apply it safely.

scenes.headline: Why you stopped getting stronger (and the fix)
scenes.narration: Same weights, same reps, same results. There is a reason, and it is fixable.

scenes.headline: Your body adapts
scenes.narration: When a workout stops being hard, your body stops needing to change. Strength comes from asking for a little more.

scenes.headline: The name
scenes.narration: The idea has a name: progressive overload. It is the steady increase of demand on your muscles over time.

definition.meaning: Progressive overload: gradually raising the demand on your muscles over time.

scenes.headline: Ways to add a little
scenes.narration: You do not have to add weight every time. Small changes count.

scenes.headline: Small and steady
scenes.narration: Add a little at a time, keep good form, and rest between sessions. Adult guidelines call for strength work on two or more days a week, so there is room to build.

scenes.headline: Pick one lever
scenes.narration: This week, change just one thing. If you have a health condition, talk to a professional first.
